label: early original-phase step 2-3, token-identity weighted (a/t/q input, first token e, previous token y)
explanation: Fires only in the original input phase at t=2 (73% of mass) or t=3 (27%). Within that window it never fires at t=0,1 or t>=4, and almost never in the delimiter step or copy phase. Whether it fires depends on which tokens are present, and the effects look additive: the current input a (9.4x lift), t (6.5x), or q (3.0x), the first token e (5.6x; also v, n, h, u), and the previous token y (4.6x). It is mostly the first occurrence of the input token (94% of mass). Its rate drops slightly with more digits in the sequence. The strongest activations come from stacked combinations such as e y [a] or n y [a]. Weaker activations come from a single favorable token, such as n y [c] or e c [k]. A t in{2,3} window gate alone gets about 100% recall but only 6.5% precision. The token disjunction raises precision to about 0.42 at 0.83 mass recall. The token weighting is graded and not cleanly boolean, so this is incomplete.
